blockers.quote: Row three. The night batch. You, copying the topper's notes. Like every night.
blockers.why: story #2: the first 7 seconds are this copying. The thumbnail is the shocked face and the crimson 0.04% chip, and that picture does not start until line 22, about 12 seconds in.
blockers.fix: Copying her notes. Like every night. Also cut line 19 to "Over every head." so the crimson chip and the 0.04% tag are on screen by about 5 seconds.

blockers.quote: That night, on the bus, the whole city is lit up. Every head. Every number. All of them moving.
blockers.why: story #11: this names what the shot already shows. I would leave here: the bat has just gone under the cupboard and nothing new happens to me.
blockers.fix: That night, on the bus. They can't see what you see.

blockers.quote: > HOLD: 2.5 s. The bus rolls through streets of chips, no numerals: a woman jogging, her chip brightening with each stride; a boy asleep on a shop counter, his dimming.
blockers.why: The viewer's week: the jogger and the boy asleep on a shop counter are not chai, the bus, exams, the office or family.
blockers.fix: > HOLD: 2.5 s. The bus rolls through streets of chips, no numerals: the coaching centre's windows still lit, the chai stall's shutter half down, chips flickering over both.

suggestions.quote: A year of fees. A year of your life. On one chair. So... keep going?
suggestions.fix: Move this to before the 2 second chair hold. At 0:30 I can already see one chair and I have heard the title, but the year and "keep going?" start just after 0:31.

suggestions.quote: > HOLD: 3 s. The ident: the title card (C) slides in on the channel's four-note signal while the camera drifts across the hall's glowing chips behind it.
suggestions.fix: Keep the four-note signal, but start the lane under it: the ball hits the wall while the card is up, so the three seconds are not only a logo.

suggestions.quote: > SCENE: A blink-long cut as the bus passes: the chai stall (the stall layers from before, plus a half-down shutter), the chaiwala dropping coins into a tin with a drawing of a second stall on it. His chip ticks up.
suggestions.fix: Line 82 already said the sixty-one is a second stall. Hang the new board and open the shutter, so this window shows the stall that happened, not the same reveal again.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
